_note: The fallback primitive (local-ai-engine.md §4.10). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) `remote` is an engine id like any other — it points at THE APP'S OWN endpoint, configured by the app, and there is no Despia endpoint for it to point at. (2) Routing to it is explicit POLICY (`local` | `prefer-local` | `remote-only`), never a confidence heuristic and never silent: every hand-off is a `routing` event a surface can show. (3) `local` policy NEVER leaves the device — with no local candidate it answers typed absence rather than quietly uploading the conversation, which is the whole difference between a seam and a backdoor. (4) The endpoint's wire shape is DATA: each remote profile declares a `dialect`, so a provider changing its API is a config edit rather than an engine release. (5) No credential ships in the app: the request carries no key, the app's backend holds them, and the fixture asserts the absence.

cases.name: remote: policy local never leaves the device
cases._note: The load-bearing negative. Nothing is installed, the policy is `local`, and a remote endpoint IS configured — the answer is still typed absence and zero outbound requests.

cases.name: remote: prefer-local falls back only when no local candidate passes
cases._note: The fallback is a policy STEP, and it announces itself: the `routing` event names the remote engine and the reason, so a UI can badge the answer as off-device.

cases.name: remote: prefer-local keeps a fitting local model and never calls out
remote: remote-only skips local resolution entirely
cases._note: Even with a perfectly good local model installed, `remote-only` does not consult it — the policy is the decision, and the reason says so.

cases.name: remote: the request carries no credential and the dialect is data
cases._note: Two pillars in one assertion. The outbound request has no Authorization header and no key field — the app's backend owns credentials — and the wire shape it speaks comes from the profile's `dialect`, so a second profile with a different dialect changes the shape without touching the engine.

cases.name: remote: an unreachable endpoint is a typed error, not a silent local retry
cases._note: Failure stays honest. The remote leg failing does not quietly fall back to a model the policy already rejected; it reports `remote_failed` and the caller decides.
